judges: (Before Dr Anita Sumanth and Sunder Mohan
judges_raw: (Before Dr Anita Sumanth and Sunder Mohan, JJ.)
respondents: Secretary to Government of Tamil Nadu Home Department and Others … Respondent(s).
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. R. Muniyapparaj Additional Public Prosecutor Assisted By Mr. M. Sylvester John
judgment_text:
PETITION filed under Article 226 of The Constitution of India praying for issuance of WRIT OF MANDAMUS or any other appropriate order or direction directing the Respondents to grant ordinary leave for 30 days without escort to the detenu, Somasundaram @ Somu S/o. Subramanian, aged about 47 years, PID 2710, detained at Central Prison, Puzhal and pass such further or other orders as this Honourable Court may deem fit to the circumstances of the case and thus render justice.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

Dr Anita Sumanth, J.:— Mr R. Muniyapparaj, learned Additional Public Prosecutor assisted by Mr M. Sylvester John, learned counsel accepts notice for the respondents and is fully armed with instructions to enable this Court to take up the matter for final disposal. Hence, by consent of both learned counsel, final orders are passed in this Writ Petition.

2. The prayer in this Writ Petition is for issuance of a writ of mandamus directing the respondents to grant ordinary leave of 30 days without escort to the petitioner's husband Somasundaram @ Somu, S/o Subramanian (convict), presently lodged in Central Prison, Puzhal. In this regard, she has given a representation on 23-3-2026.

3. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor raises a preliminary objection pointing out that the convict has just been granted 28 days leave with escort pursuant to an order dated 28-1-2026 in W.P.(Crl.) No. 697 of 2025 between 1-2-2026 and 28-2-2026. However, he would accede to the position that despite the same, if sufficient cause is made out, in terms of Rule 6 of the Tamil Nadu Suspension of Sentence Rules, 1982, the convict may be granted emergency leave.

4. Hence, let representation dated 23-3-2026 be treated as a representation seeking emergency leave and the same be disposed by the authorities in line with the extant Rules, within a period of three (3) days from today and the orders communicated promptly to the petitioner and the convict.

5. This Writ Petition is disposed in terms of this order.
